grades.reason: Covers spinlock implementations and cache-conscious spinning for mutexes. It says nothing about condition variables or why waiting on one is wrapped in a while loop.

grades.quote: If the victim process is in sleep, kkill’s call to wakeup will cause the victim to return from sleep. This is potentially dangerous because the condition being waited for may not be true. However, xv6 calls to sleep are always wrapped in a while loop that re-tests the condition after sleep returns.
grades.reason: Gives the core reason for the loop in the sleep/wakeup mechanism, which is the xv6 analogue of a condition-variable wait. A wakeup can return the waiter when the awaited condition isn't true, so sleep is always wrapped in a while loop that re-tests the condition. It doesn't name condition variables, and it explains only the kill-wakeup case.

grades.quote:
If there are more than one of them, they will all try to acquire the condition lock and re-check the condition; in many cases only one will be able to do anything useful (e.g., read all the data waiting in a pipe).

The rest will find the condition is no longer true and go back to sleep
grades.reason: Links sleep/wakeup to condition variables (wait/signal). It explains that when several waiters are woken, they all re-check the condition and only one may find it still true. The rest must go back to sleep, which motivates re-checking in a loop. It never explicitly mentions the while loop.
Covers concurrency in device drivers, interrupt handlers and locks. It doesn't address condition variables or re-testing a condition in a while loop.
